subject: Private VPC performance: latency/throughput SLOs & PoC plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@aventura-health.com>, Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@aventura-health.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC performance: latency/throughput SLOs & PoC plan

Hi Sofia / Tim —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off a short PoC:

Summary of ask (as we heard it)
- Primary requirement: deploy Redwood inference within Aventura's private VPC (no public egress for inference traffic).
- Perceived UX SLO: streaming responsiveness such that token updates start within ~200-300ms and continue at ~80-150ms per token under normal load; p95 request-to-first-byte target <= 300ms for typical 512-token responses.
- Concurrency/throughput: steady-state concurrency ~120 users, expected bursts up to ~400-500 concurrent inference sessions; average ~120 tokens per response.
- Security/compliance: HIPAA-sensitive data, SOC2 evidence required, audit logs retained per your retention policy.

Private connectivity constraints we discussed
- Preferred: Private peering (Direct Connect / Dedicated Interconnect) into the VPC — avoids NAT and public egress.
- Fallback: site-to-site VPN (IPsec) with static routes if peering not available during PoC.
- Important network details we need: public/private CIDRs for the peer, preferred MTU, whether you will allow BGP/route exchange, and expected RTT between Redwood egress point and your inference VPC.

Attachments included
- Aventura network diagram (please confirm this matches their infra) — attached as aventura-network-diagram.pdf
- Draft PoC test plan (rdw-poc-test-plan.xlsx) — outlines iperf3 + synthetic token streaming tests we propose.
- Initial SOW draft (sow-draft.docx) for timeline and milestones.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Sofia / Tim: share your network contact + current network diagram and preferred peering method by EOD Wed 9/15.
2) Redwood (Rishi / Vivek): we will send a detailed PoC checklist and temporary test endpoints by Fri 9/17.
3) Align calendar for engineering kickoff week of 9/20 (allowing 3 business days for preflight checks).

Technical open questions for your network team
- Can you confirm whether Direct Connect / Interconnect is available in the target region and if you have an existing private VIF?
- Are there any egress inspection appliances that will rewrite or proxy TLS traffic (this could add jitter)?
- Do you have maximum MTU enforced? We recommend 1500 for the PoC and to avoid fragmentation.

If this looks right I'll push the PoC plan to you and Rishi will draft the detailed test scripts. Happy to pair with your network engineer on a short call as needed.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

Subject: Re: Private VPC performance: latency/throughput SLOs & PoC plan

Monica — thanks for the thorough write-up. A few clarifications from our side (copied Tim who handles infra):

Confirmed items
- We do not want inference traffic to traverse the public internet for PHI-related calls — private connectivity only for inference endpoints.
- Typical concurrency today will be ~150, peak bursts up to ~400; that aligns with what Monica captured.
- Perceived UX target: token streaming cadence of ~100ms (best effort), and p95 first-byte <= 300ms for 512-token requests. We understand these are aggressive and want to validate via PoC.

Connectivity notes from our infra team
- We prefer AWS Direct Connect (private VIF) into our transit VPC. Account ID: 123456789012. We can also stand up a site-to-site IPsec VPN if peering timing is a blocker for the PoC.
- Enforced MTU on our side is 1500; we have a perimeter NVA that performs TLS inspection on outbound traffic to external services — however for private peering we can route inference traffic to bypass the inspection appliance.

Attachments
- Attached our current network diagram (aventura-network-diagram.pdf).

Next steps
- I'll introduce our network engineer, Tim (cc'd), who will provide the Direct Connect details and a contact for BGP setup. Expect his notes by EOD Wed 9/15.
- We will need the SOW to proceed with procurement. Can you share a short form SOW with estimated cost range?

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Director of Product, Aventura Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@aventura-health.com>, Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@aventura-health.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC performance: latency/throughput SLOs & PoC plan

Thanks Sofia — great context. A few technical clarifications and a proposed PoC testing approach so the network team has what they need.

PoC objectives (technical)- Validate end-to-end p95 first-byte < 300ms for 512-token requests over private peering.
- Validate streaming cadence under load (target ~100ms per token for the first 128 tokens under normal load).
- Confirm stability under concurrency: sustained 120 sessions + burst to 400+ for short periods.

Network/perf assumptions and budgets (initial)
- Network RTT budget: target <= 40ms round-trip between Redwood egress and your inference VPC. If RTT is higher we will see proportional increase in per-token latency for streaming flows.
- Jitter budget: target < 20ms p95; higher jitter will impact perceived streaming regularity.
- MTU: 1500 recommended (confirmed by Sofia).
- TLS: mutual TLS not required for normal PoC but we can enable mTLS for production.

Test plan (high level) — attached as rdw-poc-test-plan.xlsx
1) Baseline network tests: iperf3 (TCP and UDP) + traceroute/tcpdump from your VPC to our test endpoint. Goal: measure throughput, RTT, packet loss.
2) Synthetic streaming tests: we will run a parameterized workload that emulates real user sessions (initial short requests + streaming of tokens). We will coordinate concurrency ramps (120 steady + 400 burst).
3) Token-level latency breakdown: instrument per-token timing to separate network and inference runtime time. We will provide scripts to run on a staging instance in your VPC to generate load and capture timings.
4) Acceptance criteria: p95 first-byte <= 300ms and per-token cadence p95 <= 150ms for first 128 tokens under steady load (120), with graceful degradation under burst.

Required inputs from Aventura - BGP/Direct Connect contact details and private VIF info (if using Direct Connect).
- Staging VPC CIDR and a short-lived IAM role/service account we can use to spin up a small load generator inside your account (or permission to run a short-lived EC2 instance).
- Confirmation whether the perimeter NVA can be bypassed for the peered prefix (recommended).

Fallbacks
- If Direct Connect is not ready for the initial test window, we can run identical tests over an IPsec site-to-site VPN. Expect modestly higher RTT and jitter with VPN; we'll capture delta in metrics.

Timing proposal
- Prep: 9/15–9/17 — exchange details + configure temporary endpoints.
- PoC execution: 9/22–9/24 (3-day window).
- Postmortem: 9/25 — review results and iterate on tuning (batching/quantization/buffer sizes).

I'll attach the test plan and sample iperf/tracing commands. If the network team is available, we suggest a short 30–45 minute pairing call on 9/16 to walk through the setup.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
